newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa released from hospital.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa released from hospital.

text.p: Mother Teresa, who spent several days in intensive care late last month, was released from hospital on Friday at her own request, her doctors said.
The 86-year-old Nobel peace laureate, noted for her work with the poor and destitute, was taken to her Calcutta home from the Woodland's nursing home, where she was admitted on August 20.

"We had a plan to release her on Saturday but she was restless and wanted to go home today. We could not force her to stay one more day," Dr S.K. Sen, the nursing home's medical director, told reporters.
Dr A.K. Bardhan, Mother Teresa's doctor, said: "We have discharged her on her own request."
Mother Teresa had been admitted to the hospital nearly three weeks ago with malaria and mild pneumonia. She then suffered heart failure while in intensive care.
On Friday, she was taken from the hospital by wheelchair to an ambulance which drove her to the Mother House, headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity religious order in central Calcutta.
